rationale: Evidence: all 300 development trials so far ended off_track with no finishes. Max_error sits at 0.060 to 0.066 on nearly every design, with 1 to 2 line-loss events per run, so the robot loses the tape in bends and drifts past the 0.06 m limit. The best measured design is iteration 7 (score 125.3): 12 mm footprints, five sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 (10 mm spacing), y = 0.03, kp 3.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.35, base_speed 1.3, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12, line_loss last_direction. Every change tried from it has scored lower: widening the span alone (iteration 5), kd 0.45 (jitter, iteration 6), kp 3.5 with a narrower track (iteration 8, 108.4), a 16 mm footprint (iteration 9, 84.4), and base_speed 1.15 (iteration 10, 108.5). Iteration 10 also shows that lowering speed does not stop the line loss, so speed is not the fix. Because this is the final iteration and the final unseen-track race is scored from this design, I am not making an untested change. I resubmit iteration 7 unchanged. Expected result: about the same as iteration 7, with the oval progress near 0.6. Hypotheses to test: H1, the loss at bends comes from sensing reach, not from gain, so a sensor with more lateral reach would hold the line. H2, the 0.06 m limit is reached in a single bend before the search can recover. Measurements wanted: max_error and line_loss_events per track to locate the loss, and steering_oscillation to check jitter.
